title: The scalar quotient map on a K-flat reduction model
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell in an independent universe, a scheme W, a K-flat complex Q over the completed integral coefficient sheaf, and n >= 0. Let kappa_k be the canonical finite-reduction isomorphism [def-sf-finite-reduction-computation], d_n the scalar-adjunction quotient mate [lem-sf-integral-open-tensor-representative], tau_n the ordinary scalar quotient, and S_n the consecutive finite scalar restriction [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Then d_n(Q) followed by S_n(kappa_n) and the exact restriction localization factor equals kappa_(n+1) followed by Q(tau_n(Q)). There is no flatness assumption on the quotient coefficient ring or boundedness assumption on Q.

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the larger coefficientFiniteAdjunction Hom equivalence, then cancel the exact larger scalar-restriction localization factor. Unfold integralOpenReductionStep and coefficientQuotientNatTrans: its adjunct is the smaller derived unit followed by the inverse compactSupportSystemRestrictionComp.

Naturality moves coefficientFiniteReductionModel at the smaller level through inverse successive restriction. Expand the restriction comparison as inverse exact-localization compositor followed by the localization of coefficientRestrictionComp. The compositor and natural-isomorphism factor identities identify the resulting restriction factors. In the private finiteModel_unit calculation, transport the specified derived scalar unit normalization from homotopy localization to complex localization, using the definition of coefficientFiniteReductionModel and the exact restriction factor formula. Apply it at both finite levels.

Use uniqueness in coefficientOrdinaryQuotient_exists to identify the chosen ordinary quotient natural transformation with coefficientOrdinaryQuotientNaturalTransformation. Its mate unit equation follows by apply_symm_apply in the abstract adjunction Hom equivalence. Apply this equation degreewise and localize it. Naturality of the larger exact restriction factor and the two finiteModel_unit equations identify the two transposes; the private abstract quotient_model helper performs their cancellation. This proof uses K-flatness only through the canonical model normalization, with no boundedness or termwise-flatness assumption.

theorem integralReductionQuotientModel
    (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
    (hQ : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
      (J := ProEt.topology W) (R := completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) Q)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (integralOpenReductionStep l E W n).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes l E W (Nat.le_succ n)).map
          (coefficientFiniteReductionModel l E W Q hQ n).hom ≫
        (normalizedDVRModuleRes l E W (Nat.le_succ n)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (((scalarReductionExtension l E W n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) =
      (coefficientFiniteReductionModel l E W Q hQ (n + 1)).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex
            (coefficientOrdinaryQuotient l E W (Nat.le_succ n)) (.up ℤ)).app Q)
